prize_parts.citation: for developing methods to estimate demand and competition in differentiated-product markets from market data, making market power, substitution and merger effects empirically measurable

statement.case_for: My configuration has changed. I move from B014 to B005 with Pakes, Berry and Levinsohn. The reason is the weight I give to what a contribution lets us identify credibly. The Berry-Levinsohn-Pakes framework solved a specific problem: estimating demand for differentiated products with endogenous prices and unobserved quality, while keeping a structural link to theory. That made market power, substitution patterns and merger effects measurable in real data. Three decades of use in merger review, antitrust, regulation, trade, health and environmental analysis have tested it directly, and the sensitivity of estimates to implementation shows that it has been scrutinised, not that it is fragile. The credit for the demand-estimation core is the cleanest on the shortlist, and no member raises a timing concern. In round 1 I called B005 a methods prize and said a method is only as valuable as the questions it answers. I now think that test is met. Differentiated-product demand and market power are first-order questions for welfare and policy, and before this work they could not be answered credibly with market data. I still think B014 is a serious, mature programme. My move is not a verdict that B014 is weak. I applied the same identification and distinctness test to B014 that I applied to B005, and B014 comes out narrower. I did not move because five colleagues prefer B005, and I do not treat support counts as merit.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation about B005 is that it is a toolkit with no single headline finding, so the Committee may weigh it below substantive discoveries. The three-name cap excludes Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard and Levin, who have real claims on the broader empirical-IO tradition. BLP-type estimates depend on functional form, instruments and equilibrium assumptions, so the credibility of individual applications varies, and the citation should not suggest settled empirical knowledge about any one market. I also have to disclose a possible bias. My own work and the 2021 speech I delivered both sit in the design-based tradition, so I may over-value credible identification relative to conceptual originality, which is what B027 offers. Finally, I am not an IO specialist, so I rely on the openings of Friberg, Andersson, Strömberg and Teorell for details of the field and have not verified them.

responses.point: Hassler prefers B014 and says the overlap with the 2024 institutions prize is the main risk. He says he would move to B005 rather than defend B014 as it stands if the Committee judges that overlap decisive. He also says the within-country and state-capacity strands are less exposed to the identification critique.
responses.response: I agree that the policy-choice-under-rules agenda is distinct from the long-run origins agenda, and I made that argument myself in round 1. I now think it is a weaker defence than it looked. The strands you call less exposed to the identification critique are mainly Besley's state-capacity work. That is also the strand closest to the 2024 agenda, as Enflo says and as I conceded. The Persson-Tabellini core is the part most distinct from 2024 and the part most reliant on cross-country evidence. Whichever way the Committee cuts B014, it is exposed to one of the two objections. If the Committee wants B014, I would support a two-person Persson-Tabellini core with a citation about theory and the agenda it set, not about proven causal effects. I do not think that is the strongest configuration on the table. Your own statement that you would move to B005 if overlap proves decisive tells me our assessments of the two are closer than our rankings.

responses.point: Teorell ranks B014 second and says its constitutional and electoral-rule evidence supports a weaker causal claim than the design behind the 2024 recognition. He adds that the Committee should expect to be asked why institutions are being recognised again so soon.
responses.response: I accept your point about the identification standard, and it is the main reason for my move. I also agree that the 2024 question will come up. I disagree on one thing. I do not think the topics are the same, but the Committee would have to spend its public argument defending distinctness before it could explain the merit of B014. B005 does not face that problem. I cannot settle the discrepancy that the chair's summary flags about your stated absence of a Persson link, and I do not adjudicate it. I do note that my agreement with you on B014's identification limits does not depend on that point.

responses.point: Friberg moved his third name from Bresnahan to Levinsohn. He argues that a citation on demand estimation should credit the three authors of the paper it rests on, and he would answer the methods-prize concern by pointing to cross-field use. He also says he applies breadth of use as the common criterion and may be biased toward his own field.
responses.response: I accept the third-name reasoning and adopt Berry, Levinsohn and Pakes. I also share your concern about adjacent-field bias, so I am not relying on breadth of use alone. I add a second test, which is whether the work changed what can be credibly learned about a policy-relevant question. B005 passes it. A broad empirical-IO citation that brought in Bresnahan would be a different citation, and I would need to see it worded before judging it. I put one question to you. Is your own reservation about B014 mainly its identification or the overlap with 2024? My move rests mainly on the first.

responses.point: Hjalmarsson answered my round-1 view that B030 is only moderately mature. She says the shift-share concern concerns magnitudes and inference, not existence of the effects, and that the core finding of persistent local adjustment costs has been replicated with other designs. She grants that maturity is lower than for B005 or B014.
responses.response: I accept that distinction. The qualitative finding is well supported, and I treat the debate as about magnitudes. I still place B030 below B005 for the Committee's final public configuration. The reasons are the open question of whether the technology and trade strands form one prize motivation, and my reading that its maturity is lower. I would keep B030 in view for later years. It is not among my two alternatives now, because I judge B014 and B025 closer on the common criteria. I note that you list B005 as an alternative, so the two of us could converge, but I do not reason from that.

uncertainties: Whether the Committee prefers a narrow demand-estimation citation (Berry, Levinsohn, Pakes) or a broader empirical-IO citation that would bring in Bresnahan, Reiss, Benkard or Levin, which I cannot settle from the openings.

How a methods and measurement contribution should be weighed against substantive findings such as B014, B027 and B030. I have applied one test (did it change what can be credibly known, and was it validated in use), but others apply different tests and the Committee has no agreed comparison.

Whether the Committee reads B014 as distinct from the 2024 institutions prize. A two-person Persson-Tabellini core would reduce that exposure but might leave Besley's state-capacity strand uncredited.

How much BLP-type sensitivity to functional form and instruments should qualify the citation wording. I have not verified replication or robustness claims independently, and I rely on colleagues' statements about prior prizes, validation and citations.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile that requires recusal. The profile records no co-authorship with Pakes, Berry, Levinsohn, Persson, Tabellini, Besley, Helpman, Melitz or Redding. I overlapped institutionally at Stockholm University (2010-17) with the IIES macro group, which includes committee colleagues, and that is not a co-authorship. I note that Randi Hjalmarsson lists Bertil Holmlund as a frequent co-author and Holmlund is also my long-standing co-author. That is a committee-relationship tie and not a candidate tie, and I do not adjudicate it. My research and the 2021 presentation speech I gave as chair are in the design-based tradition, which may bias me toward credible-identification criteria, and I disclose that.
